analysis:
Both supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 2034-2597). The PR changes only documentation: a date bump and GLM5-Next text about verified weight hashing. Its patch excerpt is truncated, and the changed head ranges are not shown in these base units, so I could not review them directly.

The patch excerpt describes a behavior shift that matters to the threat model: the manifest-aggregate hash from the verified managed load (GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256) replaces separate WeightHasher passes. Coordinator-mode start registers that hash without re-reading weights while each file keeps its device, inode, size, mtime and ctime (VerifiedWeightHashStore). The load re-verifies before serving.

This is relevant to T-012 (operator replaces weights), T-027 (weight substitution) and A-004. If implemented as described, it creates a small time-of-check/time-of-use window between hash registration and load re-verification. An operator with write access could in principle change content while keeping the inode and timestamps. In practice ctime cannot easily be forged without clock manipulation, and the load verifies again before serving. The implementing code is not in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be established as a regression. No security finding is raised from documentation alone.

The base text I examined covers MiMo media and ingress, Flint constraints, Qwen4 and cache-related prose. It makes no new claims about cache scope, SSD prefix cache (T-041), authorization or encryption. Nothing in it conflicts with the threat model. The only visible changes are doc-level.

Open questions for deeper review: the actual Swift code for VerifiedWeightHashStore and ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash. They should confirm that the stat-based fast path cannot be bypassed by content swaps that preserve metadata, and that the coordinator's weight-hash check is not weakened.
